questions.question: Your neighbor's elderly father keeps getting locked out and they ask you to hold a spare key, which means being on call most evenings. Do you agree?
You got the last appointment of the week at a busy clinic, and in the waiting room you overhear someone who seems much sicker than you being told to come back next week. What do you do?
Your roommate's early alarm keeps waking you up, but it's for a job that pays for their studies. How do you handle it?
You've been saving up vacation days for a long trip, and a coworker whose child is seriously ill asks if you'd donate some of yours. How do you respond?
You're about to board a crowded bus when you notice a parent struggling with a stroller and a toddler. Letting them on first means you'll probably have to stand for an hour. What do you do?
A local shelter needs volunteers on Saturday mornings, which is the only time you have to train for a race you've signed up for. What do you decide?
Your landlord offers you a rent discount if you tell them which tenants are keeping pets without permission. Do you take the offer?
After a hectic day you realize a cashier gave you far too much change, and going back means missing your train home. What do you do?
You've found a cheaper supplier for the small bakery you run, but they're known to treat their workers poorly. Do you switch?
Your sibling asks you to co-sign a loan so they can start a business, which would put your own credit at risk. How do you decide?
A friend asks you to proofread a long application the night before your own important deadline. What do you do?
You could park in a disabled spot for five minutes to run a quick errand, and no one seems to need it right now. Do you?
Your office has one quiet private room, and you could claim it or let a new colleague who struggles with noise have it. What do you choose?
You have a spare ticket to a sold-out concert. You could resell it at a large markup or give it to a friend who couldn't afford one. What do you do?
During a heat wave you have the only working air conditioner on your floor, and a neighbor with a newborn asks to spend afternoons at your place. How do you respond?
You learn that a product you resell online is causing problems for buyers, but it's your best-selling item. What do you do?
You're asked to stay late to cover for a coworker whose parent was just hospitalized, but you have tickets to a show tonight. What do you do?
A developer wants to build affordable housing on the empty lot next to your home, and your neighborhood association asks you to sign a petition against it. What do you do?
You're circling for parking near a hospital entrance and spot the last space just as an elderly driver behind you also heads for it. What do you do?
A classmate who missed weeks of lectures because of illness asks to borrow your carefully prepared notes before an exam that is graded on a curve. Do you share them?
You've been offered a much better-paid job, but leaving now would leave your small team unable to finish a project a local community depends on. What do you decide?
Your elderly neighbor asks if you could drive them to weekly medical appointments that clash with the time you usually exercise. How do you respond?
While hiking, you meet a tired stranger who has run out of water, and you have just enough for your own return trip. What do you do?
You've inherited a family heirloom that a cousin cares about deeply, but it would be worth a lot if you sold it. What do you do?
Your team could adopt a new tool that makes your own work much easier but would make a colleague's role unnecessary. Do you push for it?
You discover that a restaurant you love underpays its kitchen staff. Do you keep eating there?
A friend who has been struggling to find housing asks to stay on your couch for a month, which would disrupt your routine. What do you say?
You could skip a long queue for a popular exhibition by asking a contact who works there to let you in through a side door. Do you?
You're the only person in your building who knows how to fix the shared laundry machine, and doing it would take your whole Saturday. What do you do?
Your manager offers you a high-visibility assignment that a colleague has been preparing for months to ask for. How do you respond?
A new parent in your building asks if you could keep the noise down in the evenings, which is when you like to play music. How do you respond?
You win a weekend getaway in a workplace raffle, and the coworker who organized the raffle hasn't had a holiday in years. What do you do with the prize?
You could buy the cheapest clothes available, knowing they are likely made under harsh labor conditions, or pay considerably more for ethically produced ones. What do you do?
You're the only one in your friend group with a car, and everyone keeps asking you for rides. How do you handle it?
A small local shop and a large online retailer sell the same item. The local shop charges more and is struggling to stay open. Where do you buy it?
You're planning a renovation that would raise your home's value but block your neighbor's only view of the garden. Do you go ahead?
A neighbor recovering from surgery asks if you could walk their dog twice a day for two weeks, which would cut into your mornings. How do you respond?
You're the only one in your family with flexible working hours, and your parents need help moving house next month. How do you respond?
Your city asks residents to cut water use during a drought, but the garden you've spent years building will suffer. What do you do?
You overhear that a colleague is about to be laid off, and warning them could get you in trouble with management. What do you do?
